title: Normalized scalar restriction squares and mate composition
statement: For commutative condensed ring-object maps a:Λ0→Λ1, b:Λ1→Λ2, c:Λ0→Λ2 with a≫b=c, any scheme map f:X→S, and any three full universal right-derived models R0,R1,R2 for lowerStar [def-sfb-diagonal-limit-interface], full-unit-normalized RestrictionSquare structures along b and c [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-scalars] exist. For every normalized square s01 along a, s12 along b and s02 along c, and every K in D(Modules Λ0 X), the scalar mates satisfy s02.mate(K)≫R2(A_X(K)) = A_S(R0(K))≫Lb_S(s01.mate(K))≫s12.mate(La_X(K)), where A is the actual scalar associator of [lem-diagonal-scalar-endpoint-composition]. No endpoints, line maps, trace equations, class maps, properness or mate invertibility are assumed.

source.place: paragraph (2), scalar associativity and compatibility of coefficient routes

proof.text: For a K-injective complex I with extended coefficients, resolve its ordinary scalar restriction by a K-injective complex J. Apply isIso_map_of_adjoints from the ringed-topos composition module to scalar extension/restriction and geometric inverse image/direct image on homotopy categories. Resolve scalar-extension tests by K-flat complexes and geometric tests by K-flat complexes whose pullback is K-flat; these resolutions exist because inverse image preserves flat objects and colimits. Scalar extension inverts K-flat quasi-isomorphisms and geometric inverse image is exact. Localized Hom into I and J is computed before localization, so the geometric direct image of the resolution map is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality and the K-injective computation of the supplied model show that its full unit on the restricted I is invertible.

Apply the proved derivedCoefficientComparison construction to the ordinary restriction/direct-image comparison and the acyclicity just established. On K-injectives both composite functors compute the same ordinary composite, so uniqueness of right-derived functors gives an isomorphism with the required full cochain-unit equation, for the supplied arbitrary universal models. This constructs the squares along b and c.

The components on underlying sheaves of the ordinary restriction compositor and of the ordinary direct-image squares are identities, so the a,b pasting equals the c square. For arbitrary supplied normalized derived squares, test their two pastings on K-injective representatives over the source coefficient ring. Cancel the invertible source unit, apply the full normalization equations (including the equation on the restricted complex, which need not be K-injective), and use naturality of the remaining unit and of the exact-derived factor isomorphisms. The ordinary identity then proves equality of derived pastings. Finally apply push_pasting_canonical to the actual scalar adjunctions; the definition of scalarCompIso identifies its endpoint comparisons, and cancellation of their inverse components gives the asserted equation.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarRestriction_comp
    {Λ₀ Λ₁ Λ₂ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1}}
    [MonObj Λ₀] [IsCommMonObj Λ₀] [MonObj Λ₁] [IsCommMonObj Λ₁]
    [MonObj Λ₂] [IsCommMonObj Λ₂]
    (a : Λ₀ ⟶ Λ₁) (b : Λ₁ ⟶ Λ₂) (c : Λ₀ ⟶ Λ₂)
    [IsMonHom a] [IsMonHom b] [IsMonHom c] (hcoeff : a ≫ b = c)
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (R₀ : DiagonalRightDerived (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ₀ f))
    (R₁ : DiagonalRightDerived (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ₁ f))
    (R₂ : DiagonalRightDerived (CondensedRing.lowerStar Λ₂ f)) :
    Nonempty (RestrictionSquare b f R₁ R₂) ∧
    Nonempty (RestrictionSquare c f R₀ R₂) ∧
    ∀ (s₀₁ : RestrictionSquare a f R₀ R₁)
      (s₁₂ : RestrictionSquare b f R₁ R₂) (s₀₂ : RestrictionSquare c f R₀ R₂)
      (K : DerivedCategory (Modules Λ₀ X)),
      (s₀₂.mate c).app K ≫ R₂.R.map ((scalarCompIso a b c hcoeff X).hom.app K) =
        (scalarCompIso a b c hcoeff S).hom.app (R₀.R.obj K) ≫
          (derivedScalars b S).map ((s₀₁.mate a).app K) ≫
          (s₁₂.mate b).app ((derivedScalars a X).obj K)
